our-squad.headline: Our gameweek 4 squad: Cole Palmer captains a 3-4-3
our-squad.standfirst: The engine's own 15 — a 3-4-3 projecting 69.57 points with the captain tripled, picked on six-gameweek horizon value, not one-week form.
our-squad.body_html:
This is the team we actually field, and it stands or falls in public. The engine optimises expected points over a discounted six-gameweek horizon on market-implied scoring rates, so every pick is a horizon bet rather than a one-fixture spike. The XI lines up 3-4-3 and projects 54.15 points before the armband; with Cole Palmer doubled that becomes 69.57.

No Haaland, by conviction rather than oversight. At his price the model wants the budget spread across three lines, and we do not pay a premium for an ownership shield. If the crowd is right about him, the consensus XI on this site owns him and will collect the evidence.

Cole Palmer wears the armband because he tops this squad's doubled projection at 15.41 — captaincy here is expected value, never narrative. Szoboszlai is vice: if the captain's match falls through, the armband moves to the next-best number, not to a hunch.

The bench, in order: 1. Sánchez, 2. E.Le Fée, 3. Bobby Thomas, 4. Shaw. It is deliberately thin — the first name is the backup keeper, and the spend sits in the XI where the points are.

distributions.headline: Gameweek 4 spreads: Cole Palmer hauls 35% of the time
distributions.standfirst: Every projection on this site is the average of tens of thousands of simulated gameweeks. This is the shape behind the average: Cole Palmer blanks in 29% of them and scores double figures in 35%.
distributions.body_html:
Cole Palmer (CHE) projects 15.41 with the armband. Behind that one number: his floor is 0 points in the worst tenth of simulations, his single most likely score is 2, and his ceiling is 16 in the best tenth. He reaches double figures in 35% of simulations and returns two points or fewer in 29%.

Saka is the alternative at 13.05 captained, on a floor of 1 and a ceiling of 15. He outscores Cole Palmer in 47% of simulated gameweeks. That comparison treats the two players as independent of each other. They are not: two attackers in the same match rise and fall together, and our simulation knows it even though this figure does not. Read it as the size of the gap, not as a settled number.

The floor and the ceiling belong to different players. Saka has the highest floor at 1 point, so he is the pick if a bad week would cost you rank. Cole Palmer has the highest ceiling at 16, so he is the pick if you need to make ground. Cole Palmer blanks least often, in 29% of simulations.

consensus-squad.headline: The consensus XI: the experts' gameweek 4 team
consensus-squad.standfirst: A mention-tally across the expert consensus sources, assembled into a legal 15 — Haaland carries the majority armband.
consensus-squad.body_html:
This squad follows the crowd on purpose. We tally which players the expert consensus sources keep naming, keep the names most lists agree on, and assemble them into a quota-, budget- and club-legal 15. The captain is the majority call, not ours: Haaland, with João Pedro as vice.

Its minutes come from sourced research notes rather than our engine — where the experts assert a starter, this squad believes them. The weekly gap between this team and our own squad measures exactly whose information about who actually plays is better.

Scored on our numbers, the 3-4-3 XI projects 47.40 points, 53.57 with the captain doubled. Both squads are published before every deadline and graded after it — the season scoreboard settles the argument.
